lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I heard a rumour, Chiron. They say you were a god, but you actually wanted to die.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: You heard right, Menippus. I could have been immortal, but here I am, dead—as you can see.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What made you fall in love with death? Most people don't find it very attractive.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: I'll tell you, since you're a thinking man. Immortality just stopped being enjoyable.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: It wasn't enjoyable to be alive and see the sun?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: No, Menippus. The way I see it, pleasure has to have some variety; it can't just be one constant state. And there I was, living forever, experiencing exactly the same things. Sun, light, food. The exact same seasons. Every single event happening in the exact same sequence, one predictably following the other. I was absolutely sick of it. True pleasure isn't just about having the same thing forever; sometimes it's about taking a break from it entirely.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fair point, Chiron. So how are you finding the underworld, now that you've moved here by choice?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Not entirely unpleasant, Menippus. The absolute equality is delightfully democratic, and frankly, there's no real difference between being in the light and being in the dark. Plus, we don't have to get hungry or thirsty like they do up top. We're completely free of all those needs.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Watch out, Chiron. You might be arguing yourself right back into a corner.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well, if the living world bored you because it was eternally, unvaryingly the same... won't the underworld bore you for exactly the same reason? Things don't change down here either. Eventually you'll need another change of scenery, a transfer to some third life. Which, I'm afraid, is impossible.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: [long pause] What is a man supposed to do, then, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Exactly what they say. Be sensible. Make your peace with the present, find contentment where you are, and decide that none of it is unbearable.
